title: Sixty Years of Being Wrong About a Bird

collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — INNER LIFE, PART X (181-200, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: An elder learns that two kinds of bird they have talked about for sixty years are really one kind.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: For sixty years, (subject) has believed that the plain brown birds and the bright blue birds that nest by the stream are two different kinds of bird. (subject.He/She) has told everyone so. Today (friend) mentions, in passing, that they're the same kind: the blue ones are the males, the brown ones are the females.

a__fx.name: Answer A
a__fx.text: (subject) stares at (friend). Then at the birds. Then at (friend) again. Then (friend.he/she) starts laughing and can't stop. "Sixty years," (friend.he/she) gasps. "I've been telling children about the two kinds of bird for SIXTY YEARS." (friend) is laughing too. (subject) goes off at once to find every child (subject.he/she) ever told, to set the record straight. It takes all week.

b__fx.name: Answer B
b__fx.text: (subject) goes down to the stream and watches the birds for the whole afternoon, as if seeing them for the first time. The blue one brings the brown one a seed. The brown one ignores it. (subject) can't believe (subject.he/she) never noticed. (subject.He/She) feels foolish for about an hour, and then delighted, because how often, at (subject.his/her) age, do you get to learn something completely new about something you've looked at every day?
